summary: DOOM: Behind the Music is a GDC talk by Doom soundtrack composer Mick Gordon that reveals how the DOOM (2016) score was developed through a radical rethinking of the brief, a culture of collaboration, and hands-on experimentation with synthesis and hardware. The talk traces the path from an initial no-guitars brief through multiple failed approaches, to a process-driven pivot that embraced experimentation, a modular analog pedal pipeline, and even guitar-based textures judiciously integrated via Morph and extended-range guitar. Key themes include fear of rejection as a barrier to change, the value of a failure-friendly team environment (including Weird Wednesday sessions), the use of unusual audio processing (ring-modulated sub-bass, tape echoes, Geiger-counter-like distortion), and the concept of a soundtrack staged as a standalone, tour-able album with deliberately chosen Doom callbacks. The speaker also discusses how game-structure and sound design can be aligned, and how controversy and subliminal ideas were navigated in pursuit of a cohesive Doom identity.
